rv.q: Crossroads Pantomimes chief executive Michael Harrison is currently overseeing more than 20 pantomimes at major venues around the country. But he always directs this gig, with one eye on talent and the other on extravagance. Robin Hood folklore has long been exploited for pantomime purposes, initially as part of the classic Babes in the Wood story.

A terrific ensemble performs song-and-dance numbers, there’s great comedy from ventriloquist Paul ­Zerdin, plus a (rather shoehorned-in) 3-D sequence. And Nigel Havers as Friar Tuck on the receiving end of Mr Clary’s waspish gags.
Clary's ability to spark off the audience and his corpsing co-stars is matchless.
Julian Clary's stale smut jokes make for a hollow and cynical evening
I wholeheartedly confess that Robin Hood has made a merry man out of me.
Julian Clary steals the show with his smut

cn.t: Julian Clary delivers gloriously over-the-top smut in this spectacular production, though eye-watering seat prices raise questions about value.
